models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Near-calm through tomorrow - Lipari to Panarea is a 3-5 kt motor-sail, no wind or sea of consequence.
briefing.synopsis: A slack, near-gradientless pattern sits over the southern Tyrrhenian: no model shows a usable breeze anywhere in the island group over the next 48 hours. Overnight at Lipari the consensus (all models sampled, 6-hourly) runs 2-4 kt backing through NE to around 307° by 06:00 Sunday, with seas and swell at 0.1 ft. Tomorrow the light flow settles WNW at 3-5 kt across the Lipari-Panarea-Stromboli triangle, still under 5 kt by Sunday evening. Monday brings the first increase, with Lipari up to 5-7 kt ESE by midday and 14 kt gusts by 18:00 (ECMWF IFS 0.25°, 04 Oct 06Z and ECMWF AIFS, 04 Oct 12Z in agreement).
briefing.overnight_anchorage: Porto Pignataro is the pick tonight - 2.1 kt N, gusts 6.2 kt, swell 0.1 ft from W, well clear of its exposed 200-250° arc (score 0.998). Marina Lunga and Valle Muria both also read sheltered, so the choice is a matter of convenience rather than safety. With wind under 4 kt and essentially no swell anywhere on the island tonight, there is nothing in the payload that would push the fleet to move.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: Sunday opens light: ICON-2i (ItaliaMeteo/ARPAE, 04 Oct 12Z, 2 km) and the ECMWF runs all show 3-4 kt WNW at Lipari at 06:00 with 0.1 ft seas. Recommended departure for Lipari to Panarea is 06:00 - 4.4 kt WNW, gusts 10.5 kt, beam reach at 86° TWA - but every window from 06:00 to 14:00 reads go and nothing deteriorates, so the fleet can leave when it suits. Expect to motor or motor-sail most of the 12 nm; breeze peaks at only 4.8 kt in the 14:00 window.

passage_notes.note: 3.3-4.8 kt WNW all day, gusts 6.8-11.1 kt, seas 0.1 ft, beam reach throughout. All windows 06:00-14:00 verdict go. Fuel plan rather than sail plan.
3.6-5.4 kt NW, gusts to 13.0 kt in the midday window, 0.1 ft seas, beam reach. All windows go; a 06:00 or 08:00 start gives the longest daylight margin on a 26 nm leg at motoring speed.

passage_notes.leg: Stromboli → Panarea, optional return (Mon 6 Oct, 11 nm, 219°T)
passage_notes.note: 3.9-5.3 kt ESE/SE, gusts 7.0-12.2 kt, seas 0.3 ft. Beam to broad reach, all windows go.

Backing S through ESE, 5.2-8.2 kt, seas building 0.8 to 1.7 ft through the day. Gusts 15-17.5 kt against means of 5-8 kt are interval-maximum values from a single model in light air. A 12:00 start gives the best breeze (8.2 kt, run) but the longest sea.
4-5 kt SSE/ESE, gusts barely above the mean (5.2-6.6 kt), seas 0.5-0.9 ft. Close reach early, head-to-wind by 14:00 - go early and sail it.

The only leg with any weather in it: 8-11 kt SSW veering W/NW, seas building 1.3 ft at 06:00 to 3.5 ft by the 14:00 window, gusts to 20.4 kt. Marked as deteriorating after 14:00, and the 14:00 departure is a no-go on forecast thunderstorms. Morning departure is the one to plan on.

cautions: Marina del Gabbiano, Stromboli, is open from every direction (0-359°) and no-anchoring - it only works while it stays calm, which the 3.2 kt N forecast currently supports, but there is no fallback shelter there if that changes.

The 14:00 Salina to Portorosa window on 9 Oct is flagged no-go for thunderstorms in the passage window; seas 3.5 ft and gusts 20.2 kt in that slot. Treat the afternoon as closed and plan a morning start.
Gust figures far above the mean in this light air are interval-maximum values from IFS and ICON-2i only - AIFS publishes no gust field - so read them as a ceiling, not a sustained condition.
Very light, shifty air means direction is less reliable than speed: stability checks show mean direction changes of 25-31° even at 0-24 h lead. Expect the breeze to wander.
